title: Binary Strings Without Adjacent Ones
statement:
Given a length `N`, count the binary strings of length `N` (strings made of the characters `0` and `1`) in which no two adjacent positions both contain `1`.

For `N = 5`, the strings `10001`, `10010`, `10101`, `01010` and `00000` are valid, while `11000`, `10110` and `11111` are not.

The count grows exponentially, so print it modulo `1000000007`.
outputFormat: Print the number of valid strings modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The valid strings are 000, 001, 010, 100 and 101. The strings 011, 110 and 111 contain two adjacent ones.

Let f(n) be the answer for length n. A valid string ends in `0` after any valid string of length n-1, or ends in `10` after any valid string of length n-2, so f(n) = f(n-1) + f(n-2). With f(1) = 2 and f(2) = 3 this gives 5, 8, 13.

hints: Track two counts for the prefix built so far: valid strings that end in 0 and valid strings that end in 1.
A 0 can be appended to anything, but a 1 can only be appended to a string that ends in 0.
Take every addition modulo 1000000007 so the numbers stay small.
